summary: Weekly POC check-in to review last week's bench runs comparing Redwood pilot vs incumbent. Redwood flagged KV cache warmup variance and a routing tail that impacted 95th percentile latency for some routes. Customer asked about dedicated slot options, VPC and KMS. Agreed to run a controlled head-to-head in Redwood lab and exchange annotated benchmarks and security docs.
topics: bench results: avg vs 95th pct latency
routing playbook and fallback to incumbent
dedicated slots and SLA for pilot
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): ok folks welcome back, umm this is the weekly gateway pilot sync. thanks for making time. Marcus and Samir from our side, Priya and team on the customer side. quick round and then dive into the bench recap.
[00:22] Priya (CTO): thanks Lena, afternoon. we had the lab results pulled in, i skimmed but want to understand the 95th percentile deltas vs our incumbent, particularly on the chat route.
[00:37] Marcus (SE): yeah great question. quick summary first — avg token latencies look similar for small prompts, but we saw a tail at p95 for the longer sequence cases. suspect cause is cache warmup and routing — some requests hit a cold KV cache plus a quant path switch on one of the replicas.
[00:56] Ethan (Lead Infra): when you say quant path switch — do you mean model was falling back to an fp16 variant or you mean runtime kernel selection?
[01:07] Marcus (SE): runtime kernel selection. our runtime will pick a slower kernel if it thinks memory pressure is high; that's what we observed in the logs. also a minority of requests got routed to a spot pool with slightly older model shard layout — that increased latency by ~120–200ms on those traces.
[01:30] Marta (ML Eng): got it, is that reproducible with your bench harness? we need to be sure it's not a noise spike in our data.
[01:38] Samir (Solutions Eng): yes we can reproduce — we ran three runs with the gateway harness and isolated by route. the spreadsheet (we'll share) shows route A (summary/extract) p95 delta +210ms vs incumbent, route B (short queries) p95 +40ms. average tps steady.
[01:58] Priya (CTO): any idea on unit cost impact if you enable always-warm KV cache vs cold starts?
[02:08] Marcus (SE): warm caches increase token efficiency because we avoid model re-compute for prefixes. cost delta depends on slot time; rough ballpark is 6–10% higher infra but reduces tail latency, so for user-facing chat flows customers often prefer the warm option.
[02:26] Oliver (SRE): for Gateway we need to quantify both, since budget is guarded. do you have numeric numbers?
[02:32] Lena (AE): we'll put concrete numbers in the annotated spreadsheet — Marcus will add a warm vs cold tab.
[02:40] Priya (CTO): also security — we need SOC2 artifacts, and confirmation on KMS/HSM integration. last time a vendor said they supported KMS but the key never left their control.
[02:53] Samir (Solutions Eng): we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) and HSM-backed wrapping. i'll attach the compliance note and a short diagram of key flow. for Redwood Private we can run the control plane in your VPC or do a peered setup.
[03:09] Ethan (Lead Infra): peering details matter — we need to know ports, IP ranges, and if you do NAT egress from your side.
[03:16] Samir (Solutions Eng): noted, we'll include a VPC peering checklist.
[03:20] Marcus (SE): back to performance — one remediation we tried is routing policy tweak: keep long-seq traffic on dedicated replicas with larger KV cache and avoid spot pool. that removes the kernel fallback and tightened the p95 by ~150ms in our informal run.
[03:37] Priya (CTO): that sounds promising. is that something you can do in Dedicated? or in Hosted trial?
[03:44] Marcus (SE): in Hosted pilot we can pin routes to a dedicated pool (soft pinning) for the duration of the test. Dedicated offering gives stronger guarantees, autoscale and committed slot behavior. for the pilot quick win we can request a short-lived dedicated slot to mirror this.
[04:02] Lena (AE): to be clear — dedicated slot request would be for the pilot window, not a commit. we can open a temporary reserved allocation for the head-to-head.
[04:11] Priya (CTO): what's the lead time for that?
[04:14] Lena (AE): 2–3 business days to provision and validate, sooner if we reuse an existing slot. Marcus will validate capacity after call.
[04:22] Marta (ML Eng): question — the p95 jump appears correlated with certain prompt prefixes. is there prefix caching behavior we can leverage?
[04:31] Marcus (SE): yes we have prefix-level caching; the issue was that some prefixes hit a low cache occupancy because our warmup scripts were missing that specific prefix distribution. we can provide a priming script that replays top-k prefixes to heat the KV/cache. that reduced p95 variance in our tests.
[04:50] Priya (CTO): can you share that script?
[04:53] Marcus (SE): yes will share in the repo, and run it live during the head-to-head so we can show delta with and without priming.
[04:59] Oliver (SRE): from infra: any networking differences that could explain latency delta? e.g. TLS termination or additional proxy hops?
[05:08] Samir (Solutions Eng): we route TLS at the edge and have configurable termination. for lab runs we use direct TLS to runtime to minimize hops; for your production config we can mirror your proxy chain in the test environment.
[05:22] Priya (CTO): excellent. another ask: provide a simple cost-comparison per-100k requests including warm cache option and quantized model variant.
[05:33] Lena (AE): yep we'll include cost model lines in the spreadsheet — Marcus we'll need to include quant variant perf numbers.
[05:41] Marcus (SE): quick note on quant: quantized variants reduce memory footprint and cost but can increase latency for longer contexts in some kernels — we saw a small penalty on path when sequence > 2048 tokens. we can show both.
[05:56] Marta (ML Eng): is your quant pipeline compatible with our tokenization? we saw odd tokenization delta in prior bench runs with another vendor.
[06:06] Marcus (SE): tokenization is model-side; we'll validate tokenization parity with your test corpus — please include the corpus sample in the traffic sample.
[06:16] Priya (CTO): timeline — we want a head-to-head by end of next week. can you make 2026-03-18 or 03-19?
[06:24] Lena (AE): propose 03-18 09:00 UTC for the lab run. Marcus will confirm tooling and Samir will set VPC peering checklist.
[06:33] Ethan (Lead Infra): 03-18 OK but need peering window confirmed by 03-16.
[06:38] Lena (AE): noted.
[06:41] Marcus (SE): small gotcha from the logs — occasional provisioning jitter when autoscale fires for sudden traffic bursts; we recommend pre-warming for burst windows or configure a mild scale-up headroom to avoid kernel fallbacks.
[06:56] Priya (CTO): we prefer pre-warm since headroom increases cost. can you quantify pre-warm duration?
[07:03] Marcus (SE): typical warm-up ~30–90s for KV cache to reach steady state depending on prefix variety; for model warm caches it's about 60s after priming. tradeoff is slot-time cost.
[07:17] Marta (ML Eng): for the head-to-head can you capture per-request traces including kernel selection flag? we want to correlate high p95 with kernel/replica IDs.
[07:27] Marcus (SE): yes, we'll enable verbose tracing for the lab run and provide a mapping file. traces will have replica id, kernel tag, cache hit/miss.
[07:36] Priya (CTO): perfect. and on the legal/procurement side — what do you need to start the pilot purchase order if we go beyond trial?
[07:44] Lena (AE): typical sequence: SOW for Dedicated/reserved slots, purchase order, and a short Terms Addendum for data residency; we can share a procurement checklist.
[07:55] Priya (CTO): ok. final recap?
[07:58] Lena (AE): recap — Marcus to share priming script and annotated spreadsheet by 2026-03-14; Samir to attach SOC2 + KMS diagram + VPC checklist; we'll schedule head-to-head 2026-03-18 09:00 UTC pending peering; Redwood to open temporary dedicated slot for that run. action items recorded and we'll follow up in email.
[08:22] Priya (CTO): thanks everyone, appreciate it.
[08:26] Marcus (SE): thanks, bye.
[08:29] Samir (Solutions Eng): thanks all.
[08:32] meeting end (rough notes: 38m)
